_notes: All records below were verified via OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, and/or Crossref API responses (queried without a mailto parameter, per user instruction), plus one WebSearch used only to locate the correct title string for Dean & Kelly (2003), which was then independently confirmed against OpenAlex and Crossref.

'abstract_summary' fields are paraphrased characterizations produced by an LLM-assisted fetch of the API response, not verbatim abstracts. Full text was not read for any paper; do not treat these as primary-source quotes.

Every doi listed was returned by OpenAlex and/or Crossref. Three (Carlson 1985, Calonico/Cattaneo/Titiunik 2014 Econometrica, Lakens 2017) were spot-checked by fetching https://doi.org/<doi> directly and confirming a 302 redirect to the publisher landing page.

One work discussed in the review (Dean & Kelly 2003) has NO doi in OpenAlex or Crossref and is therefore EXCLUDED from this file and from references.bib, per the no-invented-citation rule. It is discussed in lit_review.md with an explicit note about its verification status (OpenAlex ID W2106724377, no DOI on record).

A dedicated search for season-of-birth x myopia literature did not surface a verifiable, on-topic API record; this is reported as a search gap in lit_review.md rather than filled with an unverified citation.

A dedicated search for an existing regression-discontinuity design at zodiac cusps, or a large-N test using Mercury/Venus/Mars sign rather than sun sign, returned zero relevant records — supporting (but not proving beyond the coverage of these three APIs) the novelty claim in idea.md.

papers.title: A double-blind test of astrology
papers.abstract_summary: Double-blind test in which astrologers matched natal charts to CPI personality profiles for volunteer subjects; astrologers' match rate did not exceed chance, and their own pre-registered success criterion was not met.

papers.title: Science Versus the Stars: A Double-Blind Test of the Validity of the NEO Five-Factor Inventory and Computer-Generated Astrological Natal Charts
papers.abstract_summary: Follow-up double-blind design pairing NEO-FFI personality profiles with computer-generated natal-chart interpretations; participants could not identify their own chart/profile pairing above chance.

papers.title: The relationship between date of birth and individual differences in personality and general intelligence: A large-scale study
papers.abstract_summary: Large Danish sample (N>14,000 per the idea.md brief, volume 40 issue 7, pp.1349-1362) testing sun-sign and other date-of-birth-derived astrological variables against Big Five personality and general-intelligence measures; reported null associations. Only the OpenAlex-indexed abstract/metadata was reviewed, not the full text.

papers.title: Self-Concept in Terms of Astrological Sun-Sign Traits
papers.abstract_summary: 308 women and 114 men rated 96 astrology-derived personality traits as self-descriptive; sign-congruent self-description was found only among respondents with some astrological knowledge, supporting a self-attribution mechanism rather than a genuine sign effect.

papers.title: Belief in Astrology Inventory: Development and Validation
papers.abstract_summary: Development/validation of a Belief in Astrology Inventory in 743 Spanish psychology undergraduates; small but significant correlations between belief and extraversion, and higher belief among women.

papers.title: Intelligence and Individual Differences in Astrological Belief
papers.abstract_summary: Recent large-N study (N=8,553, US General Social Survey) finding intelligence is the largest (negative) predictor of belief in astrology, consistent with a 'superficial knowledge' hypothesis. Tests belief, not sign-trait accuracy.

papers.title: Even the Stars Think That I Am Superior: Personality, Intelligence and Belief in Astrology
papers.abstract_summary: N=264; narcissism was the strongest predictor of astrological belief, with an unexpected negative correlation between belief and intelligence measures. Tests belief, not sign-trait accuracy; modest sample size.

papers.title: The validity of astrological predictions on marriage and divorce: a longitudinal analysis of Swedish register data
papers.abstract_summary: Full-population Swedish register data (1968-2001) testing whether astrologically 'compatible' sun-sign couples marry more often or divorce less; found no consistent supporting evidence. Notable as a genuine large-N (population-register) test with a bare-null report rather than an equivalence bound.

papers.title: Are personality differences between twins predicted by astrology?
papers.abstract_summary: Precursor to the Dean & Kelly time-twins design: tests whether astrological birth-chart differences between twins correspond to personality differences. Only located via Crossref bibliographic search; abstract not reviewed.

papers.title: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Northern Hemisphere Season of Birth Studies in Schizophrenia
papers.abstract_summary: Meta-analysis of 27 Northern Hemisphere studies (126,196 patients vs 86.6M general-population births); pooled OR = 1.07 (95% CI 1.05-1.08) for winter/spring vs summer/autumn birth; effect size correlates with latitude (r=0.271, p<.005); ~3.3% attributable risk.

papers.title: Season of birth and schizophrenia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of data from the Southern Hemisphere
papers.abstract_summary: Southern Hemisphere companion meta-analysis; broadly consistent seasonal excess pattern (mirrored calendar), supporting a biological/seasonal rather than calendar-artifact explanation.

papers.title: Effects of Family History and Place and Season of Birth on the Risk of Schizophrenia
papers.abstract_summary: Danish population register (1.75M persons, 2,669 schizophrenia cases); risk highest for Feb-Mar births, lowest Aug-Sep; effect independent of family history; ~5.5% population-attributable risk for season of birth.

papers.title: Relative Age Effects Across and Within Female Sport Contexts: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
papers.abstract_summary: Systematic review/meta-analysis of relative-age effects (birth-quarter selection skew) across female sport contexts; magnitude varies by sport-specific selection mechanisms.

papers.title: The Relative Age Effect in Selection to International Team Matches in Norwegian Handball
papers.abstract_summary: 657 Norwegian handball players; relative age effect favors relatively older athletes at youth and senior international selection, with birth-quartile odds ratios ranging 1.9-8.3.

papers.title: The Benefits of Delayed Primary School Enrollment: Discontinuity Estimates Using Exact Birth Dates
papers.abstract_summary: RDD on exact birth dates around Chilean school-entry cutoff; one year of delayed enrollment lowers first-grade repetition by ~2pp and raises 4th/8th-grade test scores by >0.3 SD. Directly relevant as a precedent for exact-birth-date RDD design, distinct from our zodiac application.

papers.title: Early School Exposure, Test Scores, and Noncognitive Outcomes
papers.abstract_summary: English school-entry-rule RDD using exact birth dates; cognitive benefits at age 7 (larger for disadvantaged pupils) mostly dissipate by age 11, while noncognitive benefits persist.

papers.title: Season of birth is associated with birth weight, pubertal timing, adult body size and educational attainment: a UK Biobank study
papers.abstract_summary: ~450,000 UK Biobank participants; summer-born adults taller than winter-born by ~6.5mm (P=8x10^-9); season of birth also associated with birth weight, pubertal timing, and educational attainment, independent of the height effect. Single largest, most directly relevant season-of-birth confound paper found (multiple outcomes, huge N, smooth-in-birth-date pattern).

papers.title: Season of Birth and Exceptional Longevity: Comparative Study of American Centenarians, Their Siblings, and Spouses
papers.abstract_summary: 1,574 validated US centenarians (b.1880-1895) vs 10,885 shorter-lived siblings and 1,083 spouses; family-based conditional logistic regression; Sept-Nov birth associated with higher odds of reaching age 100 vs March birth; similar pattern in spouses, consistent with early-life/seasonal programming rather than genetics.

papers.title: Cultural Beliefs and Equity Prices: Evidence from Astrological Belief in Mercury Retrograde
papers.venue: SSRN Electronic Journal (preprint, not yet peer-reviewed)
papers.abstract_summary: Tests Mercury-retrograde belief effects on equity prices/trading behavior via cultural-belief channel. Full abstract text not retrievable through the API metadata; status noted explicitly as an unreviewed preprint, not a published peer-reviewed result.

papers.title: Finansal Astroloji: Merkür Retrosu Finansal Piyasaları Etkiler Mi? [Financial Astrology: Does Mercury Retrograde Affect Financial Markets?]
papers.venue: Kahramanmaraş Sütçü İmam University Journal of Social Sciences
papers.abstract_summary: EGARCH volatility modeling of Mercury retrograde windows (2008-2021) on BRICS + Turkish indices; mixed/weak results (positive for China/South Africa, non-significant elsewhere); BIST 100 consistent with weak-form efficiency, i.e. no significant anomaly. No permutation/exact-null approach used.

papers.title: Are investors moonstruck? Lunar phases and stock returns
papers.abstract_summary: Full/new moon effects on stock returns across international markets via regression with standard controls; a methodologically comparable astronomical-calendar-anomaly test to Mercury retrograde, useful as a design template (regression + international replication), though not itself a permutation-based exact-null test.

papers.title: Are investors moonstruck? Further international evidence on lunar phases and stock returns
papers.abstract_summary: Panel-data extension testing persistence of lunar-phase stock return effects internationally, controlling for GDP/demographic covariates.

papers.title: Robust Nonparametric Confidence Intervals for Regression-Discontinuity Designs
papers.abstract_summary: Core methodology paper: standard bandwidth-selector-based RD confidence intervals under-cover; proposes bias-corrected estimators with robust standard errors for correct-coverage inference. Foundation of rdrobust.

papers.title: Robust Data-Driven Inference in the Regression-Discontinuity Design
papers.abstract_summary: Companion software paper introducing rdrobust, rdbwselect, and rdplot Stata commands implementing the bias-corrected RD inference procedure.

papers.title: Manipulation of the running variable in the regression discontinuity design: A density test
papers.abstract_summary: Original density-based manipulation test for the running variable in RD designs; illustrated with US House election data (evidence of sorting in vote share, not electoral outcomes).

papers.title: Manipulation Testing Based on Density Discontinuity
papers.abstract_summary: Modern local-polynomial density-discontinuity manipulation test (rddensity/rdbwdensity), improving on McCrary (2008) by avoiding prebinning; directly applicable to testing whether birth dates cluster suspiciously near zodiac cutoffs.

papers.title: Interpreting Regression Discontinuity Designs with Multiple Cutoffs
papers.abstract_summary: Formal treatment of RD designs where the cutoff varies across units; derives the interpretation of the pooled treatment effect and shows naive score-normalization/pooling can waste information. Directly relevant to pooling our 12 zodiac cutoffs.

papers.title: A Practical Introduction to Regression Discontinuity Designs: Extensions
papers.abstract_summary: Practitioner-oriented extension guide covering multiple cutoffs and discrete running variables (our birth-date running variable is discrete/day-granular), complementing Cattaneo et al. (2016).

papers.title: Regression Discontinuity Designs: A Guide to Practice
papers.venue: National Bureau of Economic Research (working paper)
papers.abstract_summary: Widely used practitioner's guide to RD validity conditions, estimation, and interpretation.

papers.title: Equivalence Tests: A Practical Primer for t Tests, Correlations, and Meta-Analyses
papers.abstract_summary: Introduces the Two One-Sided Tests (TOST) procedure and smallest-effect-size-of-interest (SESOI) framework for rejecting the presence of effects large enough to matter, with practical R/spreadsheet tools.

papers.title: Equivalence Testing for Psychological Research: A Tutorial
papers.venue: Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science
papers.abstract_summary: Tutorial-level treatment of TOST + SESOI specification; argues researchers must be able to test for both presence and absence of an effect.

papers.title: Improving Inferences About Null Effects With Bayes Factors and Equivalence Tests
papers.venue: The Journals of Gerontology: Series B
papers.abstract_summary: Argues equivalence testing and Bayes factors are complementary tools for evaluating null results against pre-specified boundaries; directly supports our dual TOST+BF inference framework.

papers.title: Bayesian t tests for accepting and rejecting the null hypothesis
papers.abstract_summary: Foundational default Bayesian t-test (JZS Bayes factor) enabling symmetric evidence for/against the null, as opposed to p>.05 non-rejection.

papers.title: Using Bayes to get the most out of non-significant results
papers.abstract_summary: Practical guidance distinguishing insensitive data from genuine evidence against a theory using Bayes factors.

papers.title: Using Bayes factor hypothesis testing in neuroscience to establish evidence of absence
papers.abstract_summary: Applied Wagenmakers-school guidance (incl. prior sensitivity checks) for establishing evidence of absence with Bayes factors, aimed at practicing empirical researchers.

papers.title: Bayes factor design analysis: Planning for compelling evidence
papers.abstract_summary: Prospective design analysis for Bayes-factor studies: how to plan sample size/priors so the study is likely to yield compelling (rather than ambiguous) evidence either way.

verified_but_excluded_no_doi.title: Is astrology relevant to consciousness and psi?
verified_but_excluded_no_doi.reason_excluded: No DOI is present in the OpenAlex or Crossref record; per project rules a reference is only added to the formal bibliography if its DOI resolves. Existence, year, venue, and author names are confirmed by the OpenAlex record; the specific claims about the 'time twins' National Child Development Study design (110 variables at ages 11/16/23, sub-analysis by birth-time proximity down to 15 minutes) come from a WebSearch snippet (Skeptical Inquirer / secondary summaries), not from reading the primary source, and should be treated as provisional pending full-text access.
